focus: Explain step by step what the training actually taught students to do.

output.title: Decreasing Student Stress Through Time Management Training

scenes.narration: Alexander Häfner and colleagues tested whether a four-hour time management training program could successfully reduce perceived stress among undergraduate university students.
scenes.layout_description: A central title banner sits above an ink sketch of an undergraduate at a desk looking at a clock.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist hand-drawn black ink sketch of a university student sitting at a study desk with open notebooks, with an orange clock icon hovering above on an off-white background.

scenes.narration: The training was delivered during the middle of the semester to groups of about ten undergraduates by one trainer experienced in time management.
scenes.layout_description: A trainer stands beside a whiteboard facing a seminar circle of ten seated students.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink line illustration of a small workshop classroom with ten students seated in a semicircle around a single instructor, accented with yellow highlights on the whiteboard.

scenes.narration: The authors built a homogeneous intervention on psychological theory and empirical research, drawing directly on a training model developed by Häfner and Stock.
scenes.layout_description: A theoretical diagram links foundational psychology blocks to an overarching training framework.
scenes.visual_prompt: Sketchy black ink diagram showing three foundation building blocks labeled with psychological theory, topped with an orange arrow pointing up to a unified training blueprint.

scenes.narration: The intervention training program focused on five major components: prioritizing, setting clear goals, developing strategies, daily planning, and monitoring ongoing task completion.
scenes.layout_description: Five numbered icons form a clear linear path across the page from left to right.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn horizontal timeline with five connected circles outlined in black ink, featuring yellow accents inside the circles numbered one through five.

scenes.narration: In the first training phase, participating students engaged in self-reflection by writing down all of their current academic tasks and extracurricular activities.
scenes.layout_description: A two-column handwritten list sits on an open notepad in the center of the frame.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink drawing of a notepad showing two neat lists titled Academic and Extracurricular, with a pencil resting across the margin highlighted with orange.

scenes.narration: Next, students reflected upon the specific importance of these listed activities for their study goals, working actively to define the most important ones.
scenes.layout_description: A hand holds a magnifying glass over key items on a written page.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink illustration of a student hand using a magnifying glass outlined in black, with bright yellow star badges placed next to top priority items on a list.

scenes.narration: During this reflection, trainees answered two guiding questions: which activities are the most important, and why are these activities important to me?
scenes.layout_description: Two speech bubbles contain guiding questions flanking a contemplative student silhouette.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist black ink profile of a thinking student between two prominent speech bubbles with orange question marks.

scenes.narration: The authors noted that clarifying goals and prioritizing helps reduce harmful goal conflicts, giving undergraduate students clearer orientation in their daily academic work.
scenes.layout_description: Two conflicting crossed paths resolve into a single straight forward arrow.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink sketch of tangled black arrows untangling into a single straight path illuminated by a warm yellow compass pointer.

scenes.narration: In the second phase, students learned goal setting grounded in psychological research, defining concrete, challenging, and proximal goals for their important activities.
scenes.layout_description: An archery target stands centered with an arrow hitting near the center ring.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink line art of an archery target with an orange bullseye, surrounded by neat handwritten notes defining proximal milestones.

scenes.narration: Trainees were instructed to ask themselves precisely what they wanted to achieve in detail, actively replacing vague ambitions with explicit target outcomes.
scenes.layout_description: A blurry cloud transitions across an arrow into a crisp geometric square.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink drawing comparing a hazy scribble on the left to an organized checklist in a crisp orange box on the right.

scenes.narration: Students also defined clear deadlines for each chosen goal, ensuring their academic targets were firmly anchored to specific timeframes rather than left open-ended.
scenes.layout_description: A desk calendar displays marked dates circled with prominent rings.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn desktop calendar with specific dates circled in orange ink and small flag pins marking completion targets.

scenes.narration: In the third phase, participants developed concrete strategies to achieve their defined goals by noting down the different necessary sequential action steps.
scenes.layout_description: A staircase of progressive action blocks ascends toward a hilltop flag.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink sketch of ascending stone-like steps, each labeled with an action phrase, leading up to a goal flag highlighted in yellow.

scenes.narration: Trainees established priorities among these individual steps, planned exactly how to initiate their work, and placed special emphasis on setting proximal deadlines.
scenes.layout_description: Numbered stepping stones lead forward with immediate short-term markers.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink drawing of numbered pathway stones showing milestone markers close to the starting point, highlighted with bright orange rings.

scenes.narration: The training instructed students to mentally simulate their way to goal achievement, using an established technique to prepare their cognitive path forward.
scenes.layout_description: A student profile features an illuminated thought bubble mapping out future actions.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist side profile of a student head with a thought bubble above, containing a step-by-step pathway drawn in fine black lines with yellow glow.

scenes.narration: Through this mental simulation, trainees thought about potential obstacles that might arise and planned specific actions in advance to overcome those difficulties.
scenes.layout_description: A road with a roadblock is bypassed by a planned curving detour.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink line drawing of a small stone wall obstacle on a pathway, with an orange dotted detour line smoothly navigating around it.

scenes.narration: The fourth part focused on daily planning, where students decided what they wanted to do and when, constructing concrete schedules for their studies.
scenes.layout_description: A daily planner grid shows structured time blocks from morning to afternoon.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn daily planner sheet with time slots along the side and neatly blocked study intervals shaded in pale yellow ink.

scenes.narration: Students formulated implementation intentions, asking themselves which important tasks they should concentrate on tomorrow and when and where they would complete them.
scenes.layout_description: Three text cards show when, where, and what prompts beside a study desk.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink illustration showing a clock, a library building icon, and a book, linked by an orange ribbon representing implementation intentions.

scenes.narration: Trainees also determined how much time to schedule for each separate task and planned concrete strategies to avoid potential distractions while studying.
scenes.layout_description: An hourglass sits beside a crossed-out smartphone icon.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn hourglass filled with yellow sand next to a mobile phone with a black ink circle-backslash symbol over it.

scenes.narration: The final component instructed participants to monitor task completion each day, checking systematically what they had finished and what still needed doing.
scenes.layout_description: A checklist displays green checkmarks beside finished tasks and open boxes beside pending ones.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink clipboard with several checked boxes highlighted in orange and two empty checkboxes waiting for completion.

scenes.narration: The authors suggested that daily monitoring generates reinforcing feedback, showing students their progress clearly and potentially reducing their perceived feelings of stress.
scenes.layout_description: A upward progress curve reflects back light onto a smiling student silhouette.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink drawing of a steady upward staircase chart with yellow sparkle accents, showing visual confirmation of completed academic tasks.

scenes.narration: To verify whether students used these strategies, researchers administered an eighteen-item time management behaviour questionnaire before training and two and four weeks later.
scenes.layout_description: A timeline links three survey documents marked before, two weeks, and four weeks.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink illustration of three survey questionnaires spaced along an arrow timeline labeled baseline, two weeks, and four weeks.

scenes.narration: Trainees showed a nearly significant increase in time management behaviours after two weeks, and a statistically significant increase four weeks after training.
scenes.layout_description: A bar chart displays gradual height increases across the three measurement intervals.
scenes.visual_prompt: Three simple vertical ink bars showing scores of 3.01, 3.19, and 3.31, with an orange rising arrow over the final bar.

scenes.narration: Perceived control of time showed an upward trend at two weeks, and reached a statistically significant increase four weeks after the training.
scenes.layout_description: A gauge needle moves upward into a highlighted positive zone.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink line art of a pressure dial or meter with the indicator hand swinging into an orange zone labeled perceived control.

scenes.narration: Perceived stress, measured on the tension scale, decreased significantly two weeks after training and remained significantly lower at four weeks for twenty-three undergraduates.
scenes.layout_description: A downward slope tracks declining stress levels from the pretest baseline.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn line graph showing tension scores dropping from 3.30 down to 2.96 and 3.03, accented with yellow shaded area underneath.

scenes.narration: Meanwhile, self-reported external demands showed no significant changes across both follow-ups, supporting the conclusion that the training itself drove the observed improvements.
scenes.layout_description: A flat horizontal line representing demands contrasts with changing dependent variables.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink graph showing a flat horizontal dotted line for demands across time, enclosed in a neutral gray bracket.

scenes.narration: The training had a much stronger impact on students with no or little prior time management experience than on more experienced students.
scenes.layout_description: Two comparative bars highlight a double-sized effect for beginners over experienced trainees.
scenes.visual_prompt: Ink comparison illustration showing a tall orange bar for students with little prior experience alongside a shorter bar for experienced students.

scenes.narration: By teaching undergraduates to prioritize, set proximal goals, develop strategies, plan daily, and monitor tasks, this brief training program enhanced student well-being.
scenes.layout_description: The five training icons encircle a calm student working confidently at a desk.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn central illustration of an undergraduate student studying calmly at an organized desk, surrounded by five subtle yellow icons representing each trained skill.
